newsitem.title: INDIA: Investment skill gulf hit India power sector - Chida.
newsitem.headline: Investment skill gulf hit India power sector - Chida.

text.p: India lacks the expertise to set up the investment framework required by foreign investors in power generation, former finance minister P.Chidambaram said on Tuesday.
Indian officials, used for decades to state ownership in coal, power and railways, could not immediately change the government's framework to attract private investors, Chidambaram said.

"We must be brutally frank. I discovered in the past ten months that the government of India did not have in-house expertise to deal with the subject," Chidambaram told a business conference in New Delhi.

He cited the example of a power project involving U.S.' Enron Corp, which was hit by delays linked to questions by the political opposition on the price to be paid for power generated and other details of project implementation.
The project in the western state of Maharashtra helped the government learn about the procedures of negotiating with foreign investors, Chidambaram.

India, which launched an economic reform programme in 1991, cut back state investment in the power sector by relying on foreign investment which did not materialise. As a result, the government lost four years, Chidambaram said.
"The touching faith that the private sector will lead the way was wrong," he said.

The Indian government must revive public investment in power generation and sustain it for around five years, by which time procedural hitches in attracting private investment could be resolved, Chidambaram said.
Officials say India needs during 4,000 billion rupees ($112 billion) investment in power generation and transmission facilities during the period of its Ninth Five-Year Plan (1997-2002).
Only 10 percent of this is expected to be met with government funds, a senior official said on Monday.
